title: Australia defeats Bangladesh by innings and 51 runs as Starc takes 10 wickets in second Test
dek: Australia defeated Bangladesh by an innings and 51 runs at Mackay, with Mitchell Starc taking 10 wickets in the match. The victory draws the series 1-1 after Australia's nine-wicket loss in Darwin the previous week. The match concluded in just over two days, with Bangladesh scoring 64 and 95 in their two innings.
author: The GoCheckMySports Desk
key_fact: Mitchell Starc took 10 wickets (6-12 in the first innings, 4-39 in the second) as Australia won by an innings and 51 runs, drawing the series 1-1.
bottom_line: The series now stands 1-1 with the momentum in Australia's hands after a dominant display. Watch how both teams respond: Australia heads to South Africa in October, while Bangladesh must assess what allowed the collapse from a nine-wicket high to twin single-digit totals.
body: Australia defeated Bangladesh by an innings and 51 runs at the Great Barrier Reef Arena in Mackay, with Mitchell Starc taking 10 wickets in the match to draw the series 1-1. Victory was wrapped up just after tea on the second day, ending a match that lasted just over 125 overs, according to BBC Sport reporting it as the fourth-shortest completed Test match with a side winning.

Australia's first innings totaled 210 runs, per BBC Sport. Cameron Green top-scored with 67 runs, and Nathan Lyon added an unbeaten 32, though Shoriful Islam took 7-48 for Bangladesh. Bangladesh's first innings collapsed to 64 all out, with Starc's figures of 6-12 dominating the bowling attack.

With a first-innings lead of 146 runs, Australia put Bangladesh in again. Bangladesh fell to 24-3 inside eight overs, losing both openers early. The second innings ended at 95 all out in 38.3 overs. Starc took 4-39, Pat Cummins took 3-10, and Nathan Lyon took 3-25. Bangladesh reached 95-8 by tea before Lyon took the final two wickets.

Starc's match figures of 10-51 earned him Player of the Match and Player of the Series. Across the two-match series, according to BBC Sport, Starc took 12 wickets at an average of 12.08. Per the same reporting, Starc has moved to 10th on the all-time Test wicket list with 445 wickets, 126 wickets shy of Lyon's tally in sixth place.

The second Test marked a sharp reversal from the previous week. Bangladesh defeated Australia by nine wickets last Sunday in Darwin, per BBC Sport reporting, a loss described in the brief as one of Test cricket's greatest upsets. Pat Cummins said after the Mackay victory: "A lot of things went right these couple days and a lot of things went wrong last week. We needed to bounce back, and it was a great couple of days from the lads. I thought everyone was sharp. It was a great start and we didn't really let up after that," according to BBC Sport. Starc added: "Much better week. We knew we weren't at our best, or what we expect of ourselves, in Darwin. What we expect of ourselves this week is what we got, particularly with the ball and the wicket that aided us with the ball."
Australia's next Test assignment is a three-match tour of world Test champions South Africa in October, per BBC Sport reporting.
